templates.forfeitDescription: eight tins of sealed rations from the shelter stores
templates.description: The Supply Corps extends emergency rations against the shelter's next allocation. Eight tins, twenty days, fifteen percent. The quartermaster marks the ledger in pencil first — ink comes at signing.

templates.forfeitDescription: six jerrycans of refined fuel from the shelter reserve
templates.description: Fuel for the generator, against the shelter's word. The Corps charges twenty percent — not predatory, but the quartermaster remembers who borrows in winter.

templates.forfeitDescription: three field medical kits from the Corps dispensary
templates.description: Medical supplies on credit. The Corps keeps the rate low for medicine — dead debtors pay nothing. Fifteen days. The nurse watches the door.

templates.forfeitDescription: twelve litres of purified water from the Baron's cistern
templates.description: The Barons control the aquifer. Twelve litres, eighteen days, twenty-five percent. They do not negotiate — water is leverage, and they know it.

templates.forfeitDescription: two ceramic water filtration units from the Baron's workshop
templates.description: Filters are infrastructure. The Barons lend them at thirty percent — steep, but a shelter without clean water is a shelter that pays any price.

templates.forfeitDescription: two packs of water purification tablets from the Baron's pharmacy
templates.description: Purification tablets on credit. The Barons prefer this to lending hardware — tablets run out, and the borrower comes back.

templates.forfeitDescription: ten litres of diesel from the Guild's depot
templates.description: The Guild keeps the trains running on diesel. Ten litres, twenty-eight days. They charge less than the Barons — but default, and the tracks close.

templates.forfeitDescription: fifteen salvaged mechanical components from the Guild's machine shop
templates.description: Mechanical parts for shelter maintenance. The Guild's rate is fair — they need the shelters functional as much as the shelters need parts.

templates.forfeitDescription: one salvaged engine from the Guild's reserve stock
templates.description: An engine is capital equipment. The Guild lends one at thirty-five percent over forty-five days — long term, high stakes. Default here, and the Guild sends collectors.

templates.forfeitDescription: forty rounds of 7.62mm from the Foundry's production line
templates.description: The Foundry produces. The shelter borrows. Forty rounds, fourteen days. The Foundry does not forget — and they have enforcers.

templates.forfeitDescription: two soldering kits from the Foundry's tool crib
templates.description: Tools on credit. The Foundry charges fifteen percent — they want the shelters capable, not desperate. Default, and the next requisition goes to the bottom of the pile.

templates.forfeitDescription: three gas masks from the Foundry's protective equipment stores
templates.description: Gas masks are survival equipment. The Foundry lends three at twenty-five percent — and expects them back in working order.

templates.forfeitDescription: fifteen packs of dried rations from the Scavenger cache
templates.description: The Scavengers don't ask questions. Fifteen packs, twelve days, thirty percent. They want collateral up front — and they know what's in your shelter.

templates.forfeitDescription: five doses of antibiotics from the Scavenger's black-market stash
templates.description: Black-market antibiotics. Ten days, thirty-five percent. The Scavengers don't do instalments — pay in full, or they take what they're owed.

templates.forfeitDescription: two dosimeters from the Scavenger's salvage pile
templates.description: Scavenged dosimeters, sold on credit. Twenty days, twenty-five percent. The Scavengers know the value of what they lend — and the value of what they'll take.

consequences.description: The creditor notes the default. Standing drops — not catastrophically, but the ledger remembers.
A serious default. The creditor's standing drops sharply, and word spreads — other factions take note.
The creditor suspends trade relations. Fourteen days of closed markets — the shelter must find supplies elsewhere, or negotiate a settlement.
Default damages standing AND closes the creditor's markets. Ten days of embargo, a lasting reputation hit, and the threat of escalation.
The creditor posts a bounty. Collectors may visit — not an army, but enough to remind the shelter that debts have consequences. Escalation looms.
The creditor seizes pledged collateral and sends a warning. The shelter loses the asset but keeps market access — for now.
Unresolved debt escalates to a shelter raid. The creditor's enforcers arrive — this is not negotiation. Standing damage is severe and lasting.
The creditor invokes a labor clause. Seven days of compulsory service — the shelter loses a survivor's labour but keeps market access and avoids escalation.
A treaty-backed debt defaults. This is not just a broken promise — it is a diplomatic incident. Standing collapses, and the treaty itself is at risk.
In rare circumstances — humanitarian crisis, prior service, faction doctrine — the creditor absorbs the loss. Standing improves slightly. This does not happen twice.
